extracted.intended_audience: authors, copyeditors, indexers, and publishers preparing and editing manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, copyediting, and producing books, journals, and electronic publications, including punctuation, names, citations, numbering, indexing, pagination, and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names, personal — capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: names, personal, capitalization of, 8.3-18
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed guidance on capitalization of personal names including particles, unusual capitalization, Asian/Burmese/Chinese/Dutch/French/German/Hungarian/Indian/Indonesian/Italian/Japanese/Korean/Portuguese/Russian/Spanish/Thai/Vietnamese treatments; overview and resources. See also treatment of epithets, nicknames, patronymics, pseudonyms, stage names, and titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names, personal — forms, variants, and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: handling of patronymics, shortened names, possessive forms, plurals, pseudonyms, stage names, screen names, epithets and nicknames, titled persons, sovereigns and rulers, saints
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules and cross-references for indexing and word-division (e.g., 2-em dash for omitted names, hyphenation, plurals and possessives of names), and guidance for variants and resources on names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names, proper — definition, capitalization, and hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: proper names defined (5.6) and guidance on capitalization, compound forms, hyphenation, plurals, possessives, and use as words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers generic terms with proper names, headline-style capitalization, hyphenation of compounds containing proper names, real vs. metaphorical uses, vessels and vehicles, and variants; see also indexing of abbreviations derived from proper names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English names and materials — treatment and permissible changes
rubrics_metrics.description: non-English materials: overview (11.1) and treatment in English context (11.3-5); permissible changes to non-English materials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on capitalization, punctuation, permissible editorial changes, IPA notation, special characters and tables, titles of works in various languages, glossing and translations, and indexing of non-English names and words; includes language-specific notes (Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Hebrew, Japanese, Korean, Latin, Russian, Spanish, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of works — formatting and source citation treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: titles: use in building or award names, indexing of titles, italics vs roman, plurals, titles in source citations and in running text
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on italics for titles (14.86), titles in bibliographies and notes, titles in non-English, short forms and subtitles, use of titles instead of author names in notes, and page-numbering conventions for titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes — basic structure and format
rubrics_metrics.description: notes, basic structure, 14.20; format of notes and note numbers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers basic note structure, numbering and format (14.24-28), placement, cross-checking, formatting for multiple citations, continued notes across pages, note reference numbers/symbols, formatting of notes in tables, proofreading, and generic markup; includes examples and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes vs. endnotes and electronic considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: footnotes not always used in electronic publications; footnotes vs endnotes guidance (14.43-48, 14.49-51)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses when to use footnotes vs endnotes, relation to electronic formats and continuous-publishing models, alternatives for e-books, and accessibility/navigation issues for online publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes and bibliography system — elements and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: notes and bibliography system overview (14.19-23); elements to include and flexibility of the system
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the structure of notes-and-bibliography citations, relationship to author-date system, disciplines that use it, elements to include, examples and acceptable variations, and how notes relate to bibliographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citations — page numbers and locators
rubrics_metrics.description: page numbers in source citations: general guidance and exceptions for e-books and electronic formats (14.22, 14.160, 14.174, 15.23)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for including page numbers in notes and author-date citations, treatment for chapters, journal articles, classical works, ff. and passim, forthcoming works, reprints, e-book locators, and legal-style citations; how page numbers interact with volume numbers and ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened citations and ibid.
rubrics_metrics.description: shortened citations in notes and use of ibid. and similar short forms (14.19, 14.29-36, 14.34)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to form shortened citations, when to use ibid., examples and variations, cross-references to full citations, and discipline-specific practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and management of notes — avoiding excessive notes
rubrics_metrics.description: length considerations for notes and remedies for excessive notes (14.40, 14.56-60)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on reducing the number and length of notes, use of abbreviations, consolidating citations, moving editorial content to bibliography or text, and other strategies to avoid overlong or excessive notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbers and pagination — general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: page numbers (folios) and pagination: appropriate use, determining page 1, fixed vs reflowable electronic pagination, and pagination for multivolume works
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers standards for folios in books and e-books, blind (unexpressed) page numbers, cross-checking, page numbering in tables of contents and running heads, how to mark pages in manuscripts and proofs, and avoiding repagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page ranges — en dash, condensing, and index locators
rubrics_metrics.description: page ranges: use of en dashes, condensing, and use as index locators (6.78, 9.60, 16.100-113)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on formatting ranges with en dashes, condensing long ranges, using ranges in journal and book citations, ff. vs ranges, and use of page ranges in running heads and indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers — when to spell out vs use numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: numbers: basic principles, general rule and alternative rule, and considerations of consistency, flexibility, and readability (9.1-9.4)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chicago’s general rule on spelling out vs numerals, an alternative rule, special cases for dates, times, ages, ordinals, centuries, and beginning sentences; emphasis on consistency and readability and when exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and numerals — formatting with units, separators, and special uses
rubrics_metrics.description: uses of numbers with units of measurement, decimals, fractions, percentages, large numbers, money, and technical enumerators (9.13-9.25, 10.49-10.56)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for spacing and separators (commas, spaces), use with abbreviations and symbols, hyphenation rules in compound terms, ratios and percentages, telephone numbers, and percentages/monetary conventions; references to SI units and International System of Units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinal numbers and numbered entities
rubrics_metrics.description: ordinal numbers: format, hyphenation, day-of-month usage, and usage in named streets, military units, and personal names (9.6, 9.47, 9.51)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to form ordinals (nd, th, rd), hyphenation and compounding rules, and treatment of ordinal numbers in legal citations, place names, and titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses and punctuation with parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: parentheses usage and punctuation guidance (6.95-98)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to punctuate sentences containing parentheses, placement with other punctuation (commas, periods, colons, question/exclamation marks), back-to-back parentheses, font and typographic concerns, uses in citations and tables, parentheses in source citations and translations, and marking proofs for parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthetical elements in sentences — integration and style
rubrics_metrics.description: parenthetical elements in sentences and how they function (6.48, 6.51, 6.85, 6.95)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on parenthetical elements (clarifications, translations, glosses), punctuation and sentence flow, and marking and formatting in proofs and manuscripts. See also uses in index glosses and explanatory material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oxford (serial) comma — Chicago preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Oxford (serial) commas: Chicago’s guidance and usage (6.19-21, 6.23, 8.165, 14.135)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chicago Manual preference for serial comma in lists and related punctuation implications; examples and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation of compound terms and numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: hyphenation rules for compound terms, participial phrases, noun-plus-numeral compounds, and numerals in compounds (7.89 sections cited)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which compounds require hyphens, hyphenation sections for various compound types (sec. 1–4), and special cases such as open compounds, phrasal adjectives, and hyphenation with numerals and ordinal forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing — alphabetizing, locators, and special entry treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: indexing: alphabetizing rules, entries beginning with numerals, indexing of names, non-English words, abbreviations, and page locators (16.x series)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on alphabetizing personal and organization names, particles, non-English names, treatment of initials and abbreviations, use of locators (page numbers and ranges), cross-references, glosses in index entries, run-in style vs display entries, and index proofreading/checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running heads and headers — use and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: running heads and their placement including endnotes and page ranges (1.15, 1.16, 2.76, 14.47)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on text used in running heads, including use of page ranges, part titles, and how running heads interact with pagination and endnotes for books and chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online publications — functional features and citation differences
rubrics_metrics.description: online publications: navigation, hyperlinks, PDF use, front/back matter, indexes and reference-work treatments (1.118-1.123, 14.233, 14.267)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features for online publications (navigation, screen margins, PDFs for distribution and proofs), hyperlink and metadata practices, differences in citation and pagination for e-books and websites, and special considerations for wikis and continuous publication models.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF files — role in manuscript submission and proofing
rubrics_metrics.description: PDF files as edited-manuscript formats, annotations, prepress proofs, and content proofs (1.118, 2.71, 2.107, 2.133, 2.140)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PDFs for manuscript submission and proofs, annotate and mark changes in PDFs, use PDFs for continuous publishing and e-journals, and consider PDF limitations for reflowable formats and indexer usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations in non-English contexts — punctuation and typographic style
rubrics_metrics.description: quotations in various languages: French, Greek, Russian; punctuation and typographic styling of quotations in translations and non-English contexts (11.3, 11.19, 11.28-32, 11.101, 11.116)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on language-specific quotation marks (guillemets, etc.), punctuation placement around quotations, typographic conventions, and permissible editorial changes when translating or quoting non-English material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes: numbering, placement, and citation integration
rubrics_metrics.description: note numbers, citation placement, keyed notes, and formatting across text and bibliography (14.24-28, 14.53, fig. 14.6)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to number notes, where to place note numbers/symbols in text, use of keyed notes and line/page locators, ordering multiple notes, notes in tables and captions, and cross-checking notes with bibliographies and text citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent and related punctuation conventions across contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: punctuation conventions across parentheses, brackets, colons, semicolons, and their interactions with citations and translations (6.97-101, 11.12, 14.37-38)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for nested punctuation, punctuation inside translated quotations and bracketed material, use of brackets for glosses, and interactions with scholarly abbreviations and legal citation punctuation.
